instructions: Describe a registered compatible method, submitted object, actual findings, defensible conclusion and limitations. Preserve sample provenance and planned outcomes.
Similarity or class characteristics do not individually identify a person. A no-findings result is inconclusive, not proof of innocence.
Do not force a culprit match, fabricate a measurement or change a forensic finding to repair a story.
contract: Input, method, duration, result identities, findings and supported matches stay consistent with the immutable plan.
Every positive identification names its individualizing basis and readable supporting material.
Rookie has no interactive forensic workflow; higher levels obey their planned forensic topology.
positiveExample: The export confirms a device account was active; the report states that account activity alone does not identify the operator.
negativeExample: A blurred face is reported as a conclusive identity match, or a negative test exonerates a suspect.
criteria: Scientific confidence matches the method and object rather than narrative convenience.
No invented numerical accuracy, database hit or chain-of-custody event.
Inconclusive results and alternative explanations remain explicit.
